title: Explorer parameters on large instances, long runs (round 2)
question: Which explorer settings (count, rate, heuristic exponent, deposit) give the lowest cost on the large Table I instances when runs are long (1,500 iterations)?
hypothesis: From round 1: the default (n2_r0.05_b0.5_d0.05) stays among the best and is hard to beat; n2_r0.05_b2_d0.05 led round 1 (-0.189% vs -0.160%) with a gap that kept widening through the run, so it is the most likely to beat the default; deposit 0.02 does not help except possibly at rate 0.02; the gain is on T9/T10, not on T8.
analysisPlan: Round 2 of the two-round race begun in pecto-explorer-tuning-r1: same instances, budget and code, seeds 5-9 (15 new paired runs per setting). n1_r0.05_b0.5_d0.05 was dropped after round 1 (worse than the best round-1 setting, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.041). n0 is rerun because it is the reference of every gap. Final best cost as the paired gap to n0 on the same instance and repeat. The decision uses rounds 1+2 pooled (30 paired runs per setting): mean gap, 95% interval, exact paired Wilcoxon; this round's summary alone is a replication check (same ranking? same per-instance pattern, T8 flat?). Secondary: anytime gap curves (does the b2 gap keep widening late?) and final diversity, as tie-breakers.
decisionRule: Pool rounds 1 and 2 (30 paired runs per setting). Choose the setting with the lowest mean gap to n0; if it is not significantly better than the default n2_r0.05_b0.5_d0.05 (exact paired Wilcoxon on the 30 per-run gap differences, p < 0.05), keep the default. Among statistically equal settings prefer the one with higher final diversity.
